Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options & sizing — AuroraEdge

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together three pragmatic reservation options that balance predictable throughput with cost flexibility. High level — each option includes: cluster topology (GPU type & count), a minimum guaranteed GPU floor, and a 12-week ramp schedule with checkpoints for usage-based flex.

Summary (details attached):
- Option A — Conservative floor
  - 8 x A800 (min guaranteed 8 GPUs)
  - baseline throughput for inference-heavy, low-batch latency needs
  - 12-week ramp: 8 -> 16 (week 6) -> 24 (week 12)
- Option B — Market-entry (recommended)
  - 16 x A800 (min guaranteed 12 GPUs)
  - balanced for mixed generation + embeddings; includes KV cache warming plan
  - 12-week ramp: 12 -> 16 (wk4) -> 24 (wk10) with 2-week burst windows
- Option C — Growth posture
  - 32 x A800 (min guaranteed 24 GPUs)
  - higher throughput, reserved burst lanes for peaks
  - 12-week ramp: 24 -> 32 (wk8) -> 32+burst

Decommit / guardrail notes (short):
- Soft floor for first 30 days with credits if usage is below 70% of guaranteed floor.
- Automated staging: we recommend a prewarm window before any scheduled ramp to avoid cold-cache penalties.
- Fallback model variants: lightweight quantized variants for graceful degradation during moments of constrained capacity.

Next steps: if you can indicate which option (A/B/C) maps closest to AuroraEdge’s expected Q1 volumes, I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben to finalize SLA language, pricing, and DocuSign-ready attachments.

Attaching a short proposal + GPU runbook for your procurement team.

Best,

Mike — good questions. See answers below and a compact table you can paste into procurement. Marissa/Ben, looping you in to scope pricing and SLA language.

Quick answers:
- Min guaranteed vs cluster topology: we express guarantees in whole-GPU units (no vGPU slicing for committed floors). Option B (16 x A800) has a contractual minimum of 12 whole GPUs reserved. The remaining 4 GPUs are capacity that can be used as burst (subject to availability).

- Ramp triggers (recommended hybrid model):
  - Time-based milestones: automatic tranche unlocks at week 4 and week 10 contingent on no usage or security flags (default unlock unless an operational alert exists).
  - Usage-based clause: if average sustained utilization across guaranteed GPUs >= 65% over a 7-day rolling window after week 4, then next tranche is considered "in-use" and will be billed; if <65% we hold the tranche and provide a 2-week evaluation period.

- Soft-floor credit mechanics (example):
  - Example: contracted floor = 12 GPUs month. If actual averaged utilization across the month is 60% of the floor, AuroraEdge receives a pro-rated credit equal to 40% of the monthly floor commitment for that month, capped at 25% of the monthly invoice. Credits are issued automatically on the following billing cycle.

- Isolation & VPC: yes — Dedicated pools can be assigned to a customer-managed VPC endpoint (Private mode). For AuroraEdge PII-handling lanes we recommend keeping the most sensitive models pinned to a Private deployment. That is an additional add-on and we can surface pricing in the attached proposal.

Compact table for procurement (copy/paste):
- Option B (recommended): Cluster: 16 x A800; Contracted floor: 12 GPUs (whole GPUs)
  - Ramp schedule: Week 0 — 12 GPUs active (prewarm); Week 4 — gated unlock to 16 (time-based; auto unless operational hold)
  - Utilization-trigger: 65% 7-day rolling utilization to auto-escalate additional tranches after time gate
  - Soft-floor credit: pro-rated credit up to 25% cap if floor utilization <70%
  - VPC isolation: Supported (Private dedicated add-on)

Attachments: updated proposal with explicit MLP language and a runbook that shows prewarm windows and cache-warm steps.

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm price per GPU-hour & draft the DocuSign-ready MSA with the above ramp triggers? Ben — please confirm if we should recommend a 2-week prewarm for cache population or a 1-week for AuroraEdge workload (they run heavy embedding refreshes daily).

Thanks — Aditya
